description: Helper permission rules and containment definitions for Firstmate host

bash_policy.admitted_why: Direct script-file execution allows leaf command auditing and avoids shell-wrapping vulnerabilities
bash_policy.denied_why: Inline code execution flags and command-position substitutions permit uninspected arbitrary execution

system_telemetry.why: Read-only inspection of host RAM, CPU, disk, process list, and files for health and lane hygiene sweeps

version_control.why: Repository status, worktree creation, commit history, and diff inspection for agent tasks

agent_toolchain.why: Inter-agent CLI execution, provider quota checks, secret detection, package operations, and remote host checks

firstmate_lifecycle.why: Session initialization, automated test execution, ShellCheck installation, and linting

lean_ctx_builtins.why: Core context-reduction engine primitives for compressed file reads, AST searches, and session status

deny_rules.why: An agent must never call the herdr CLI directly. Splitting the coordinator pane stacks worker panes on the operator's visible screen, and raw send-text/send-keys into a pane bypasses the sanctioned send path. This is the documented rule in docs/audits-20260928/AGENTSEC.md 3.5, and it also closes the HIGH gap 5.1 (the Pi hook only intercepted 'herdr pane split', never send-text/send-keys). Use the wrapper scripts instead: bin/fm-spawn.sh creates a worker pane and bin/fm-herdr-agent-report.sh reports the agent state.

minimax.deny_rules_note: The mcode permission matcher treats a command pattern as a prefix on the FIRST command token, so 'herdr:*' refuses every direct herdr invocation from an agent turn. Script-file invocations such as 'bash bin/fm-herdr-agent-report.sh' are NOT affected, because their first token is 'bash'. This was proven in a live mcode run: 'herdr pane list' was refused by the rule and 'bash bin/fm-herdr-agent-report.sh working' ran normally.
minimax.prohibited_write_roots_note: The prohibited secret roots apply to write_roots as well as read_roots. A blanket write to a secret root is never admissible; the drift check fails closed on it.

pi.why: Extension loading and npm package resolution in agent directory
